content:
Apple has cited a recently stayed securities fraud lawsuit in support of its request to pause further proceedings in the lower court Epic Games legal battle while the Supreme Court weighs in on portions of the dispute. Here's what's happening.

Apple referenced the relevant ruling as Judge Rogers considers the request to stay the lawsuit.

Earlier this year, a proposed class action lawsuit on behalf of the City of Coral Springs Police Officers' Retirement Fund was filed, accusing Apple of securities fraud.

The lawsuit alleges that Apple misled investors regarding whether the company was truly complying with the Epic Games injunction, and whether it would roll out its announced AI-driven Siri features.

Meanwhile, Apple continues to fight the contempt of court ruling in the Epic case. The Supreme Court is now considering whether Apple can be held in civil contempt for collecting commissions on purchases made outside of the App Store—a practice not explicitly prohibited by the 2021 injunction that required Apple to allow outside purchasing options.

Last week, Apple requested that the lower court pause proceedings to determine what commissions, if any, Apple can collect on purchases outside the App Store while the Supreme Court reviews the contempt ruling.

Apple argued that arguments that could be affected by the Supreme Court's decision in the contempt matter have already been challenged by Epic Games in the lower court proceedings.

In fact, Apple has already made a similar request to stay the Coral Springs securities fraud case, as it also touches on the Epic Games case.

Earlier, Judge Wise granted Apple's request, meaning the Coral Springs case will remain stayed until the Supreme Court rules on the civil contempt ruling.

That decision prompted Apple to cite Judge Wise's ruling in the Epic Games case to the court, arguing it supports its request for Judge Gonzalez Rogers to stay the relevant proceedings.

Here's an excerpt from Apple's petition to Judge Rogers:

Judge Rogers is currently weighing Apple's arguments in favor of staying the case alongside Epic's arguments against it. Apple is hoping Judge Wise's decision will convince Judge Rogers to make the same call.

Notably, in its reply to Epic's opposition to staying the case, Apple has also asked Judge Gonzalez Rogers to issue a temporary freeze on the relevant proceedings even if she denies the stay request, allowing Apple to petition the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court to maintain the stay during the appeal while the Supreme Court also reviews the contempt ruling.
